texts.preamble: Anantha Kumar vs The Commissioner on 25 June, 2025 Author: S.Srimathy Bench: S.Srimathy W. Before The Madurai Bench Of Madras High Court Dated : 25.06.2025 Coram: The Honourable Mrs.Justice S.Srimathy W.P(MD)No. 17155 of 2025 and W.M.P(MD)Nos.13021 to 13023 of 2025 Anantha Kumar . vs. 1. The Commissioner, Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration, Dms Campus, 5th Floor, No.359, Annasalai, Teynampet, Chennai - 6. 2. The Food Safety Officer, Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration Department, Food Safety Wing, Virudhunagar District. 3. The Designated Officer, Aruppukottai Municipality and Region, Virudhunagar District. Prayer : Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of Indi praying for issuance of a Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus to call for the pertaining to the impugned order passed by the 3rd respondent herein in Na.Ka.No. 1099/A1/UPaaThaSa/2025 dated 05.06.2025 and quash the same as illegal and consequently direct the respondents to deseal the petitioner's Aathiyappan Petty Shop at Aruppukottai Main Road, Therkupatti, Palavanatha Aruppukottai, Virudhunagar District. 1/5 Anantha Kumar vs The Commissioner on 25 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24363450/ 1 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 26/06/2025 08:24:43 pm ) For Petitioner : Mr.J.Mohamed Ibrahim For Respondents : Mr.S.Shanmugavel Additional Government Pleader, f Order The present Writ Petition has been filed for the issuance of a Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus to quash the impugned order passed by the 3rd respondent in Na.Ka.No.1099/A1/UPaaThaSa/2025 dated 05.06.2025 and consequently direct the respondents to deseal the petitioner's Aathiyappan Petty Shop.
texts.facts: 2. The petitioner runs a small petty shop selling fruits and other food items. The respondents have alleged that the petitioner is selling banned items, namely tobacco. This is the third time the respondents have imposed fine. In the previous two instances, the petitioner paid the appropriate fine, and the shop was allowed to reopen. 3. In the present case, now the petitioner contended that the respondents without seizing any material has sealed the shop. Moreover, no notice was issued. 4. On instructions, the learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for respondents 1 and 2 submitted that 195 grams of tobacco were https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis The respondents have not clarified whether the tobacco was kept for personal consumption or for commercial purposes. Since the quantity is considered a consumable amount, this Court is inclined to quash the impugned order.
